subject: Q4 sprint: Sales pipeline cleanup + new commit criteria workshop
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Sales Ops <ops@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Q4 sprint: Sales pipeline cleanup + new commit criteria workshop

Team —

Quick heads-up: as we wrap Q4 we need a focused sprint to clean up stale pipeline rows and align on the revised commit/best-case/pipeline definitions from Finance. The updated definitions are attached (Commit_Definitions_v2.pdf) and I pulled together a 30-min workshop to walk through the practical changes and the verification checklist.

Please do the following by EOD Thursday:
- Update Stage for any deals that have been 'stagnant' > 60 days (see checklist in deck)
- Flag deals you believe should move from Best Case to Pipeline or vice versa in the HubSpot link below
- Add a one-line justification on the deal record for any commit changes (required for forecasting audit)

Workshop details:
- When: Thu 12/17 10:00–10:30 PT (calendar invite being sent)
- Who: Affected AE + sales manager mandatory; ops invited
- Purpose: Walk through Commit_Definitions_v2 and go through 4 live deal examples (including ACME)

Why this is urgent: Finance needs a clean commit set for the Q4 close to avoid last-minute adjustments. If we don’t tighten the definitions now, we risk upward noise in the pipeline that will push wrong expectations into the forecast.

Attachments: Commit_Definitions_v2.pdf, Sprint-Cleanup-Deck.pptx
Links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/ACME

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Senior Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Sales Ops <ops@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 10:03:11 -0800
Subject: Re: Q4 sprint: Sales pipeline cleanup + new commit criteria workshop

Thanks Irene — good plan. A few quick notes from my side:

1) I'll pre-tag the deals in my book that meet the >60d stagnation rule and add the one-line rationale as requested.
2) For any large ACV deals (>$250k) we should escalate to the revenue leader before moving commit status — suggest adding a short approval step in the checklist.
3) Can we record the workshop? Ops may want to reuse the deck for other regions.

On the recording: agreed, please record and drop into the sales enablement folder. Also, I looked at the v2 defs — the Commit vs Best Case distinction is clearer, but we should add an explicit guidance bullet for 'TPR events' (third-party review) that often pushes deals back into Pipeline.

Karthik
Director, GTM Ops

From: Ellen James <ellen.james@acme.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Sales Ops <ops@acme.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 11:27:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Q4 sprint: Sales pipeline cleanup + new commit criteria workshop

Hi Irene —

Thanks for the heads-up and for including ACME in the live examples. Quick confirmation: we will have our procurement review on 12/21 which may change the close date — is it OK if we remain in Best Case until procurement completes? If Finance needs it in Pipeline now, I can ask procurement for an expedited review but wanted to make sure we align on the definitions first.

Also: attached our internal timeline (ACME-Procurement-Timeline.pdf) — it might help as you go through the workshop.

Cheers,
Ellen James
Senior Procurement Manager
ACME Corp

[Attachment: ACME-Procurement-Timeline.pdf (pdf)]
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen James <ellen.james@acme.com>, ACME Sales Ops <ops@acme.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q4 sprint: Sales pipeline cleanup + new commit criteria workshop

Thanks Ellen — appreciate the note and the timeline. Short answer: keep the deal in Best Case until procurement completes if the procurement step is the primary gating item and you’ve documented the expected completion date on the deal record. Finance is asking that any time-based hold be documented so we can exclude it from an active commit reclassification.

Action items from workshop (recap):
- Marissa: review the 5 deals in the 'staggered close' bucket and add one-line justifications by Monday 12/21
- Karthik: add the escalation step for $250k+ deals to the checklist doc and version it in the enablement folder
- Sean: coordinate recording upload and create short 5-min highlights clip for managers
- ACME / Ellen: keep Best Case and add procurement expected close in the HubSpot deal timeline field

Thanks everyone for moving quickly on this. If anything changes for your book, ping me directly.

Irene
Senior Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
